chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi'l Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ja'far al-Azdi, from Amr ibn Abi'l Miqdam. He said: I heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) say:

Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi once, God repels from him one thousand hateful things of this world and one thousand hateful things of the Hereafter. The least of the hateful things of this world is poverty, and the least of the hateful things of the Hereafter is the punishment of the grave.

key_terms.آية الكرسي: Ayat al-Kursi (Verse of the Throne) — Quran 2:255, one of the most revered verses describing God's sovereignty
key_terms.عذاب القبر: Punishment of the grave — the suffering experienced in the intermediary state (barzakh) before Resurrection
key_terms.مكروه: Hateful/harmful thing — something detested or afflicting

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards of reciting Ayat al-Kursi according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) describes the immense spiritual reward for reciting Ayat al-Kursi (Quran 2:255), the Verse of the Throne, even just once. The hadith quantifies the protection in vivid terms: one thousand worldly afflictions and one thousand otherworldly afflictions are averted. By identifying poverty as merely the lightest worldly affliction and the punishment of the grave as the lightest affliction of the Hereafter, the Imam highlights the magnitude of divine protection offered through this single Quranic recitation.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
al-Baqir (the one who splits open knowledge)
